Red flower Kenaf

This plant is one of my favorite to grow. A must have for all those who want to grow something both decorative and edible.

As the name implies, it looks very similar to Marijuana. So if you have nosy neighbors, it is best to let them know you are NOT growing weed.

This plant is BEAUTIFUL, a real show-off. There is also a white flower variety that is used to make rope and very strong fibers.

This plant can be grown from seeds or cuttings. Cutting take very easily and will root even without hormones within 3 to 4 days!

This plant can be used to feed livestock or even eaten in soups, salads, curries. It does not fry very well. The amazing part is that they contain up to 30% PROTEIN! An excellent plant for all you vegetarians and vegans.

The flower can be used to make a beautiful purple dye as well.

It does well as a potted plant if you have a place for it in the sun. In colder climates, they can be started indoors and will grow VERY quickly once transplanted.

They are EXTREMELY pest resistant (never seen it get attacked) and need very little water, perfect for those of you that live in arid climates.

It is an annual and can produce a great many seeds. The oil pressed from the seeds is quite delicious and nutritious. The cake (after you have pressed the oil out) can be used as a green manure or be fed to livestock.

A plant that you just put in a sunny place and forget.

For those of you who raise rabbits, chickens and other livestock, this plant REPLACES commercial feed! At 20-30% protein you don't need to supplement their diet with anything else.

The leaves can be dried in the sun and kept in a cool dry place to feed your animals during the winter.

Each plant will grow to about 5 feet tall.

It is best to plant them 2 by 2 at a distance of 12 inches between plants.

Makes for a fast growing hedge.

Use gloves if you process this plant for leaf or seed, it tends to leave you with small prickles

As someone who grew up hunting in Africa and has been on several lion hunts before id like to say this story was bullshit from the start. Almost all lion hunts are cunducted off bait from a blind. Lions like other predatory cats are most active at night and therefore aby collar or special tagging would have been inpossible to see, especially in the short time frame you have to line up a good shot, while barley moving a muscle so as to not spook it. As much as people want to be upset, no one realizes that without hunting these animals are essentially worthless, except to poachers, and often very destructive to their own habitats and young. Everything about this hunt was completely legal and the fact that theres even a debate about it is ridiculous.

Tl;dr hunting and conservation go hand in hand, and its more than likely that killing and old male lion saved several cubs that it would kill upon finding a new pride.
